External benchmark

GIAC GAIPS objective alignment

A documented comparison between the academy’s published lessons and GIAC’s current AI Platform Security objectives. The mapping identifies areas of coverage and curriculum development priorities.

Explore the technical course

Independent curriculum mapping. Intellica is not affiliated with GIAC. This comparison uses public objectives and is not an endorsement, an accredited preparation course, or a prediction of exam performance. Confirm the current exam rules directly with GIAC before booking.

Current published exam information

Checked 2026-11-25.

Exam
One proctored examination
Format
GIAC lists CyberLive performance-based virtual-machine testing for GAIPS.
Length
54 questions; 2 hours
Passing score
65% for exam versions released on or after 25 July 2026
Objectives
Eight published outcome areas, including agentic systems, AI foundations, architecture, infrastructure, risk, MLOps, retrieval and model customisation.

GIAC states that exam specifications may change. The candidate portal is authoritative for the version attached to an individual attempt.

Priority curriculum development

Two objective areas require additional lessons and labs: development pipelines and MLOps security (Model pipelines: data, training, registry and signing) and model customisation and alignment (Fine-tuning, adapters and alignment: poisoning, backdoors and limits). The academy will not claim full GAIPS coverage from topic titles alone. Each mapped area requires measurable outcomes, original lab evidence, original practice items and independent review.

Related GIAC AI credentials

GIAC’s wider AI portfolio provides distinct benchmarks for platform security, offensive testing and security automation.

  • GAIPT (AI Penetration Tester): published objectives include direct and indirect injection, RAG, agents, MCP, API security and AI architecture flaws. The page is marked presale; Level 5 uses it as a benchmark, not an available credential.
  • GASAE (AI Security Automation Engineer): practical automation across offensive, defensive and cloud security operations; relevant to Level 4.
  • GOAA (Offensive AI Analyst): a distinct offensive AI benchmark covering AI-enabled reconnaissance, vulnerability discovery, social engineering and operational security.

Reviewed 2026-11-25. Intellica is independent of GIAC, ISC2, ISACA, CompTIA, CSA, IAPP, OWASP, MITRE and NIST. Mappings show how our lessons relate to published objectives. They are not an affiliation, an approval or a prediction of any exam result.
